McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the underside of the car, reshaping the floor to get a cleaner, more consistent airflow that sticks the car to the track. They’ve also refined the rear‑corner inlet, smoothing out the air that feeds the diffuser for a bigger boost off the exits. Together, these changes should give the car a tighter grip and stronger push‑through on the straights, helping the drivers extract more lap time this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the underside of the RB‑engineered floor, reshaping the surfaces that sit next to the side‑pods to match the latest fence adjustments. The new profile should smooth airflow and give a modest boost in rear‑end stability, especially through high‑speed corners. In short, the change aims to keep the car planted and maintain its edge on a circuit where every ounce of downforce counts.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has tweaked the underside of the car – reshaping the floor’s main panel, smoothing the curvature of the side fences, and fine‑tuning the edge wing – plus a subtle re‑profile of the engine cover’s top deck. These aerodynamic tweaks tighten airflow under the car, giving a bit more down‑force and stability in fast corners, which could translate into better grip and quicker lap times on this weekend’s circuit.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the underside of the car – reshaping the floor, adding new little fences and re‑contouring the floor edge – plus refined the inlet on the sidepods to smooth airflow. These changes tighten the aerodynamic “tunnel” under the chassis, giving the car a bit more down‑force without adding drag, which should help it stick to the track and improve corner speed this weekend. In short, the tweaks are all about grabbing a little extra grip where it counts most on the next race.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have rolled out a new front‑wing layout for the weekend, tweaking the flap shape to give the car a more adaptable balance that suits the particular demands of this circuit. The change should boost front‑end grip and make the car easier to turn through the high‑speed corners, helping the drivers extract more performance without sacrificing straight‑line speed. In short, a sharper, more versatile front wing means better handling and a stronger shot at the podium.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has reshaped the in‑board floor fences, moving the leading edge farther inboard and giving the panel a smoother, three‑dimensional curve that eases back into the original shape. This tweak helps clean up the airflow under the car, boosting down‑force and stability through corners. In practice it should give the drivers a more predictable rear end and a little extra grip for qualifying and the race.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber/Audi have tweaked the forward section of the floor, reshaping it to spread the load more evenly and give the car extra rear‑end grip on the straights. They’ve also introduced a new front‑wing flap that can be dialed in for the specific demands of the circuit, helping to smooth out the car’s balance through the corners. Together, the changes should make the car stick better to the track and be easier to drive fast over this weekend’s layout.
